Rashi on Shabbat 62b:10:1.english: They would urinate - For he deduces [this] from [the word] seruḥim.

Rashi on Shabbat 62b:13:1.hebrew: לידי עניות - דאמרינן בע"פ (פסחים דף קיא:): שרא דעניותא נביל שמיה, ונביל קרי ליה, ואוהב מקום מיאוס; ומשתין מים לפני מטתו — היינו מיאוס:
Rashi on Shabbat 62b:13:1.english: To [a state of] poverty - For we say in [the chapter entitled] Arvei Pesachim (Pesachim 111b): The angel of poverty, his name is Nabil; and it calls him Nabil [because] he loves a place of filth; and urinating before his bed — that is filth.

Rashi on Shabbat 62b:13:2.hebrew: ערום - אורחא דמילתא נקט: מתוך שהוא ערום, אינו יוצא לחוץ להשתין, דטורח הוא לו ללבוש ולצאת:
Rashi on Shabbat 62b:13:2.english: Naked - It mentioned the typical case: since he is naked, he does not go outside to urinate, as it is a bother for him to get dressed and go out.

Rashi on Shabbat 62b:14:1.english: However, [facing] outward, we have no [concern] with it - For the stream is long and splatters far away.

Rashi on Shabbat 62b:16:1.hebrew: משא ולא משא - שאינו רוחץ ומשפשף יפה, אלא מעט מים, כגון רביעית מצומצם:
Rashi on Shabbat 62b:16:1.english: Washes and does not wash - That he does not wash and rub [his hands] thoroughly, but rather [uses] a small amount of water, such as an exact revi'it [quarter-log].

Rashi on Shabbat 62b:18:1.english: Over matters of her ornaments - That he does not want to buy [them] for her.

Rashi on Shabbat 62b:19:1.english: Are haughty - That is, [with an] upright stature.

Rashi on Shabbat 62b:19:2.hebrew: ותלכנה נטויות גרון - שהיו הולכות עקב בצד גודל, למעט בהילוכם, שהיו מסתכלין בה והיא שוהה בפסיעותיה. ודרך נוטין גרון לילך בנחת, לפי שאינו רואה לרגליו:
Rashi on Shabbat 62b:19:2.english: And walk with outstretched necks - That they would walk heel to toe to reduce their pace, so that [people] would gaze at her as she lingered in her steps. And it is the way of those with outstretched necks to walk slowly, because one cannot see one's feet.

Rashi on Shabbat 62b:19:3.english: “And wanton eyes,” that they would fill [their eyes with] kohl - [This is] an expression of sikra [red paint].

Rashi on Shabbat 62b:19:6.hebrew: הלוך וטפוף שהיו מהלכות ארוכה בצד קצרה - שתראה צפה על ראש חברתה, והוא נוי לה. ונשואות היו, לפיכך מספר בגנותן:
Rashi on Shabbat 62b:19:6.english: “Walking and mincing,” that they would walk a tall [woman] alongside a short [one] - So that she would appear [as if] floating above the head of her companion, and this was an adornment for her. And they were married women; therefore, [Scripture] speaks of their reproach.

Rashi on Shabbat 62b:19:7.english: And mincing [ve-tafof] - Like: “Because you caused [others] to float [and drown], they caused you to float” (Avot 2:6).

Rashi on Shabbat 62b:19:8.hebrew: תעכסנה - כמו וכעכס אל מוסר אויל (משלי ז׳:כ״ב), והוא ארס של נחש. וקרי לה עכס על שם שאינו מטילו אלא על ידי כעס:
Rashi on Shabbat 62b:19:8.english: Making a tinkling [te’akasna] - Like: “And as an ekhes to the discipline of a fool” (Proverbs 7:22), and it is snake venom. And it is called ekhes because [the snake] only discharges it by means of anger [ka’as].

Rashi on Shabbat 62b:19:9.english: In an angry [snake] - An angry snake.

Rashi on Shabbat 62b:1:1.hebrew: ומאי רבי מאיר - היכא אשכחן דאיירי בה רבי מאיר בלא רבנן, ופליג רבי אליעזר עליה:
Rashi on Shabbat 62b:1:1.english: And what is [this statement of] Rabbi Meir - Where do we find that Rabbi Meir dealt with it without the Rabbis, and Rabbi Eliezer disagrees with him?

Rashi on Shabbat 62b:1:2.hebrew: בד"א - דרבי אליעזר פוטר, והאי פוטר היינו מותר לכתחלה, כדאוקימנא:
Rashi on Shabbat 62b:1:2.english: In what [case] is this said - [Regarding that] which Rabbi Eliezer exempts; and this "exempts" means permitted ab initio, as we established.

Rashi on Shabbat 62b:20:1.english: Decaying sores - As in: “His flesh shall rot away” (Zechariah 14).

Rashi on Shabbat 62b:20:3.hebrew: נקפים - חבורות, לשון המנקף רגלו, וניקף סבכי היער (ישעיהו י׳:ל״ד):
Rashi on Shabbat 62b:20:3.english: Bruises - Wounds; an expression [similar to] “one who strikes his foot,” and “and the thickets of the forest shall be cut down” (Isaiah 10:34).

Rashi on Shabbat 62b:20:4.english: They would adorn themselves - That is the hair, which they comb and style.

Rashi on Shabbat 62b:20:5.english: They would adorn themselves - [The word mitkashtot] is similar to [the word] miksheh, like a sort of notarikon.

Rashi on Shabbat 62b:20:6.hebrew: פתיגיל - נוטריקון: פתח גילה — אותו מקום:
Rashi on Shabbat 62b:20:6.english: A fine dress [petigil] - [It is] an acronym [notarikon]: petach gilah [an opening of joy] — that place [i.e., the pudenda].

Rashi on Shabbat 62b:20:7.english: For instead of beauty - For all these will come upon you instead of your beauty.

Rashi on Shabbat 62b:20:8.hebrew: כיבא - קיוטור"א, ליחה — כמו שיחנא וכיבי דקדושין דפלימו (דף פא:):
Rashi on Shabbat 62b:20:8.english: A sore [kiva] - [In Old French,] cuiture [a burn or ulcer], [exuding] pus, as in “boils and sores” in Kiddushin, [in the story] of Pelimu (81b).

Rashi on Shabbat 62b:22:1.english: Their secret parts - [This is] like their orifices.

Rashi on Shabbat 62b:22:2.english: Will empty - Like: “And she emptied her pitcher” (Genesis 24[:20]).

Rashi on Shabbat 62b:22:3.english: That they were poured out like a jug - [They were] discharging the blood of a flux [zivah].

Rashi on Shabbat 62b:22:4.english: Like a forest - They became filled with hair, and [became] repulsive for marital relations.

Rashi on Shabbat 62b:23:1.english: People of arrogance - [They would] speak in the language of arrogance and mocking speech.

Rashi on Shabbat 62b:23:2.english: [Did] you dine - [This refers to] marital relations.

Rashi on Shabbat 62b:23:4.english: [Bread] that is not well-kneaded - A virgin.

Rashi on Shabbat 62b:23:5.hebrew: פת עמילה - ברייאיא"ה בלע"ז:

Rashi on Shabbat 62b:3:1.hebrew: כשיש בה בושם - פלייטון יש בההוא חומרתא העשויה כקמיע, דכיון דיש בה בושם — תכשיט היא לזו שריחה רע; ולמשלף ואיתויי נמי לא חייש, כדאמרן: דגנות הוא לה:
Rashi on Shabbat 62b:3:1.english: In a case where there is perfume in it - [That is,] there is foliatum in that knot made like an amulet; for since there is perfume in it, it is an ornament for this [woman] whose odor is foul, and he is also not concerned about [her] removing [it] and carrying [it], as we said, for it is a disgrace for her.

Rashi on Shabbat 62b:3:2.hebrew: אבל אין בה בושם - חומרתא לחודא לאו תכשיט הוא, וחייבת:
Rashi on Shabbat 62b:3:2.english: However, [if] there is no perfume in it - The receptacle alone is not an ornament, and she is liable.

Rashi on Shabbat 62b:4:1.hebrew: זאת אומרת - הא דקתני: "אין בה בושם חייבת", אלמא דקסבר רבי אליעזר: המוציא אוכלין בשבת בכלי פחות מכשיעור — דלא מיחייב על הוצאת אוכלין פחות מגרוגרת, כדלקמן (שבת דף עו:) — חייב מיהא על הכלי, ולא אמרינן: הכלי טפל להן ולא מיחייב עליה, שלא נתכוין להוציא אלא משום אוכלין. ופלוגתא היא על סתם משנה השנויה בפרק המצניע (לקמן שבת דף צג:), דקתני: "פטור אף על הכלי":
Rashi on Shabbat 62b:4:1.english: That is to say - [From] that which was taught, "[If] it has no perfume in it, she is liable," it follows that Rabbi Eliezer holds: One who carries out food on Shabbat in a vessel [in an amount] less than the [requisite] measure — for which he is not liable for carrying out food [of an amount] less than a dried fig, as [stated] below (Shabbat 76b) — is nevertheless liable for the vessel; and we do not say [that] the vessel is subordinate to them and he is not liable for it, since he intended to carry out only on account of the food. And this is a dispute with an unattributed mishnah taught in the chapter [entitled] Hamatznia (below, Shabbat 93b), which teaches: "He is exempt even for the vessel."

Rashi on Shabbat 62b:4:2.hebrew: דהא אין בו בושם כפחות מכשיעור דמי - שהכלי קלט את הריח, ושיעור הוצאת בשמים בכל שהוא, וכיון שאינו כל שהוא — הוי ריחה פחות מכשיעור (הוא). וקתני חייבת, ולא אמרינן נעשה כלי טפל לריח שבתוכו, ואריחא לא מיחייב דפחות מכשיעור הוא:
Rashi on Shabbat 62b:4:2.english: Since [the case where] there is no perfume in it is comparable to less than the [requisite] measure - For the vessel absorbed the fragrance, and the [requisite] measure for carrying out perfume [on Shabbat] is any amount, and since it is not [even] any amount, its fragrance is [considered] less than the [requisite] measure. And it teaches [that] she is liable, and we do not say: Let the vessel become subordinate to the fragrance inside it, and for the fragrance one is not liable because it is less than the [requisite] measure.

Rashi on Shabbat 62b:5:1.hebrew: ושאני הכא - ליכא למימר נעשה כלי טפל לריח, שאין בו שום ממש, ואפילו פחות מכשיעור לא מיקרי. אבל פחות מכשיעור בדבר שיש בו ממש — נעשה כלי טפל לו, ופטור:
Rashi on Shabbat 62b:5:1.english: And it is different here - One cannot say that the vessel becomes secondary to the scent, which has no substance whatsoever, and it is not even called "less than the [requisite] measure." But [with] less than the [requisite] measure of something that has substance, the vessel becomes secondary to it, and he is exempt.

Rashi on Shabbat 62b:6:1.english: The chief ointments - The choicest of oils.

Rashi on Shabbat 62b:7:1.english: Issued a decree - Due to the sorrow over the destruction [of the Temple].

Rashi on Shabbat 62b:7:2.hebrew: ואי אמרת - זה פלייטון, והאי קרא בתענוג משתעי — שלא היו נותנים לב לדברי הנביאים הניבאים על הפורענות, ועסוקים בתענוגים:
Rashi on Shabbat 62b:7:2.english: And if you say - [That] this is balsam oil, and this verse speaks of pleasure — that they would not pay heed to the words of the prophets prophesying about calamity, and [instead were] occupied with pleasures.

Rashi on Shabbat 62b:8:1.hebrew: ולטעמיך הא דכתיב - בהאי ענינא "השותים במזרקי יין", ורבי אמי ורבי אסי פירשו: זהו קנישקנין — כלי זכוכית ארוך ולו שני פיות, ויין נזרק מזה לזה:
Rashi on Shabbat 62b:8:1.english: And according to your reasoning, that which is written - In that [same] passage: “That drink wine in mizrekei” [Amos 6:6], and Rabbi Ami and Rabbi Asi explained: This is a kenishkanin — a long glass vessel that has two spouts, and wine is thrown from one to the other.

Rashi on Shabbat 62b:8:2.hebrew: שמזרקין - על ידי אומנות, כדאמר בהחליל (סוכה דף נג.): ״מטייל בתמני כסי״:
Rashi on Shabbat 62b:8:2.english: That they throw - Through [acrobatic] skill, as it says in [the chapter entitled] Hechalil (Sukkah 53a): “Juggling with eight cups.”

Rashi on Shabbat 62b:8:3.english: Is that also prohibited - To drink nowadays from a kenishkanin?
